newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gensec details Randex shr offer.
newsitem.headline: Gensec details Randex shr offer.

text.p: Genbel Securities (Gensec) is offering minority shareholders of its mining development subsidiary Randex 270 cents a share, the company announced on Wednesday.
However, it said in a statement shareholders might also elect to receive 4.91 new Gensec shares for every 100 Randex held or a combination of cash and Gensec shares.
"After due diligence investigations by Randex's advisors, we feel that 270 cents is a fair offer," Gensex and Randex chief executive Anton Botha said.

"However, as the principal reason for the offer was our belief that the Randex assets could be more effectively utilised within Gensec, we felt that Randex shareholders should be offered the opportunity to benefit from continued investment with Gensec," he said.

"Our first choice would have been to unbundle and distribute Randex's assets to shareholders. However, various legal and tax complications made unbundling a sub-optimal approach and shareholders would have been prejudiced," Botha said.
A fair and reasonable offer to minority shareholders, based on independent evaluations was the only other meaningful option, he added.
Gensec shares were last quoted at 60.25 rand on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, unchanged from Tuesday's close, while Randex shares were up 10 cents at 270 cents. Gensec holds 64 percent of Randex.
